message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference list of the **long‑weekend holidays that Canadians can enjoy in 2023**.  
(“Long weekend” means the holiday falls on a weekday and the adjacent weekend days give you at least three consecutive days off.)

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Typical Long‑Weekend Pattern | Provinces/Regions that observe it |
|---------|-------------|------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| **Family Day** | **Feb 20** (Monday) | Monday + weekend → 3‑day break | Alberta, British Columbia, Saskatchewan, Ontario, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, Newfoundland & Labrador (except Quebec, Manitoba, Yukon, Northwest Territories, Nunavut) |
| **Good Friday** | **Apr 7** (Friday) | Friday + weekend → 3‑day break | All provinces & territories |
| **Victoria Day** | **May 22** (Monday) | Monday + weekend → 3‑day break | All provinces & territories |
| **Labour Day** | **Sep 4** (Monday) | Monday + weekend → 3‑day break | All provinces & territories |
| **Thanksgiving** | **Oct 9** (Monday) | Monday + weekend → 3‑day break | All provinces & territories |
| **Christmas Day** | **Dec 25** (Monday) | Monday + weekend → 3‑day break | All provinces & territories |

### Notes & Quick Tips

1. **New Year’s Day (Jan 1)** – 2023 fell on a Sunday, so there was no extra day off.  
2. **Canada Day (Jul 1)** – 2023 was a Saturday; the statutory holiday is observed on Monday, Jul 3, but that does **not** create a long weekend.  
3. **Remembrance Day (Nov 11)** – 2023 was a Friday; it gives a 3‑day break only if you take the preceding Thursday off.  
4. **Boxing Day (Dec 26)** – 2023 was a Tuesday; it does not create a long weekend unless you take the following Monday off.  

Feel free to plug this table into your holiday‑planning app. If you need province‑specific details (e.g., “Family Day” is not observed in Quebec or Manitoba), let me know!
